lesson_title: They Got Their Land Back, and Kept It Wild
hook_text: In 1998, a community won back land inside the Kruger. They had a choice: farm it, or keep it wild.
clip_script: In 1969, the Makuleke people were forced off their land in the far north of the Kruger. Nearly thirty years later, they won it back. They could have ploughed it or built homes. Instead, they kept it wild, partnering with tourism companies to build lodges. Now the land earns rent, young people train as guides and rangers, and baobabs and elephants still roam. That's community conservation: when people own and benefit from nature, they protect it. Add eco-tourism, travel that cares for nature and local people, and conservation becomes a livelihood.
visual_style: Archive-style map of the northern Kruger; a community meeting; a lodge among fever trees; a young guide pointing out elephants to visitors.
pacing: A historical opening, a choice, then a confident outcome.
